newsitem.title: USA: Unocal sees UNO-VEN deal complete in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Unocal sees UNO-VEN deal complete in Q2.

text.p: Unocal Corp said Thursday it doesn't expect its deal to sell off the company's U.S. Midwest assets to state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) for $250 million to be wrapped up until the second quarter.
Unocal and PdVSA said in December the deal would go through by the end of the first quarter, "but this is going to slip into the second quarter," a Unocal official said Thursday.
Unocal and PdVSA signed a letter of intent last December as part of Unocal's strategy to exit the U.S. downstream oil industry and divide its upstream operations into U.S. and international units.

Unocal agreed last November to sell the bulk of its downstream assets, including its West Coast network of 1,350 retails sites and three refineries, to Tosco Corp in a deal worth $2 billion to Unocal. That transaction is expected to be complete by the end of March.
If the deal goes through, Unocal will own the partnership with $250 million in cash.

PdVSA subsidiaries will acquire a 153,000 bpd refinery near Chicago, Illinois, which has a relationship network with some 200 wholesalers and supplies 2,500 independently-owned "76" branded retail outlets across 15 states in the Midwest and eastern U.S.
PdVSA also will acquire a lubricants blending plant in Cincinnati, Ohio and storage terminals across the region covered.
The refinery will run Venezuelan crude oil shipped to the U.S. Gulf and transferred by pipeline.
